title: Distributed Martian Atmospheric CO₂ Processing Swarms: A Conceptual Architecture for Plasma-Vortex ISRU and Autonomous Microreactors
description: A speculative concept study exploring distributed swarms of autonomous ultralight atmospheric microdevices for Martian CO₂ processing using compact plasma-vortex reactors. The manuscript distinguishes demonstrated evidence, literature-supported mechanisms, engineering extrapolation, and long-horizon speculation, and frames the architecture as a falsifiable research hypothesis rather than a validated mission design.
notes: Concept paper. Stage 1 examines distributed physicochemical CO₂ processing using compact plasma-flow reactors. Stage 2 is a substantially more speculative protected biological micro-habitat extension and is not proposed as an open biological release under current planetary-protection constraints.
method: Concept generation and systems-engineering analysis combining literature-supported mechanisms, first-order thermodynamic and mass-flow calculations, architecture comparison, evidence-tier classification, and a staged experimental validation roadmap.
